speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, everybody, I'm Jeff.
zh: 嘿,大家好,我是 Jeff。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess I was introduced, but I'm the co-founder of Exa, and today I'm gonna give a talk on turning go-to-market into an AI engineering problem in the spirit of this AI engineering affair.
zh: 我猜刚才已经介绍过我了,我是 Exa 的联合创始人,今天我要做一个演讲,主题是把 go-to-market(市场推广)变成一个 AI 工程问题,以契合这场 AI 工程活动的精神。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just a quick show of hands just to understand the audience.
zh: 先快速举手调查一下,了解一下观众情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Raise your hand if you're technical.
zh: 如果你是技术人员,请举手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, great, okay.
zh: 好,很好,好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I kind of oriented this talk around go-to-market as presented to engineers, so I'm happy that I did that.
zh: 所以我把这个演讲定位为面向工程师的 go-to-market,我很高兴我这么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool, so first, just to ground what EXA is, because it's sort of relevant inside of this presentation, EXA is a search engine for agents.
zh: 好,首先,先说明一下 EXA 是什么,因为它和这个演示的内容有点相关,EXA 是一个面向智能体的搜索引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think like, agents are really smart, but they don't have access to the web.
zh: 想象一下,智能体非常聪明,但它们无法访问网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're like this web MCP, web tool that agents can access.
zh: 我们就像一个网络 MCP、一个智能体可以访问的网络工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: We power Cursor, we power Cognition, we power a lot of the AI ecosystem at this point.
zh: 我们为 Cursor 提供支持,为 Cognition 提供支持,目前为 AI 生态系统的很大一部分提供支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: And before we start, I also just want to talk about, especially as a technical audience, why should you even care?
zh: 在开始之前,我也想谈谈,尤其是对技术观众来说,你为什么要在乎这个?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why should you care about go-to-market?
zh: 你为什么要关心 go-to-market?

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess this audience cares about go-to-market because you chose to go to this go-to-market talk.
zh: 我猜这个观众关心 go-to-market,因为你们选择了来听这个 go-to-market 演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think there's this funny narrative right now, which is people are like, oh, product is the only thing that matters, or distribution is the only thing that matters.
zh: (勘误:此行应保持原编号)你要找出关于目标对象的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's all sorts of Twitter flame wars.
zh: 而且 Twitter 上有各种各样的骂战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, oh, is Clueli going to succeed because they're really good at distribution, but they're like, what the heck is their product?
zh: 比如,哦,Clueli 会成功是因为他们真的很擅长分发,但他们的产品到底是什么鬼?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then other people are like, oh, the product needs to be super good because agents shop for the product, so they'll shop for the best product.
zh: 然后另一些人说,哦,产品必须超级好,因为智能体会挑选产品,所以它们会挑选最好的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so my view and my experience in the last few years is that
zh: 而我的观点和过去几年的经验是:

speaker: Unknown
en: You just kind of have to do both.
zh: 你基本上必须两者都做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I think you have to get product right and you have to get go-to-market right.
zh: 我认为你必须把产品做对,也必须把 go-to-market 做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you got to build the thing.
zh: 你得把东西造出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's got to be good.
zh: 它得是好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you got to get it into people's hands.
zh: 然后你得把它送到人们手中。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't do both things, then you don't have a company.
zh: 如果你不同时做到这两件事,你就没有一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's kind of my view on the matter.
zh: 这就是我对这件事的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would say, like, a really funny thing also is, like, as a technical person, when you start a company or you start some sort of project,
zh: 我想说,还有一件非常有趣的事是,作为一个技术人员,当你创办一家公司或开始某种项目时,

speaker: Unknown
en: Like very much so the bias is like, hey, I'm going to just build the thing.
zh: 倾向性非常明显,就是:嘿,我就只管把东西造出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm gonna make it really, really freaking good, right?
zh: 我要把它做得非常非常厉害,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's kind of like the bias you have as like an engineer.
zh: 这基本上就是你作为工程师的倾向。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the bias we had when we started Exo and we were like honestly pretty bad at go to market.
zh: 这就是我们创办 Exo 时的倾向,而说实话,我们当时很不擅长 go-to-market。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we were not doing enough marketing, we were not doing enough sales.
zh: 我们做的营销不够,销售也不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think the cool thing about go to market, particularly in 2026, is you can treat go to market like an engineering problem and particularly an AI engineering problem.
zh: 但我认为 go-to-market 的酷之处,尤其是在 2026 年,是你可以把 go-to-market 当作一个工程问题来对待,尤其是当作一个 AI 工程问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that's a super exciting thing.
zh: 所以我觉得这是一件非常令人兴奋的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's more fun for engineers than ever to do go to market, because you can automate things.
zh: 对工程师来说,做 go-to-market 比以往任何时候都更有趣,因为你可以自动化很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do so much as one person, et cetera.
zh: 一个人可以做非常多的事情,等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, I want to make this interactive.
zh: 另外,我想让这个演讲有互动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: If anybody has questions at any point, please ask, because I'm aware there's a lot of talks, and I don't want to bore you.
zh: 如果任何人在任何时候有问题,请提问,因为我知道演讲很多,我不想让你们觉得无聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool, so the hypothesis I have is if you're an engineer, or if you're anyone, you can treat go-to-market like an engineering problem.
zh: 好,我的假设是:如果你是工程师,或者你是任何人,你都可以把 go-to-market 当作一个工程问题来对待。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first, I guess, what do go-to-market teams do?
zh: 那么,首先,go-to-market 团队都做些什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have a laundry list of things here, of things that go-to-market teams do, but here are a few.
zh: 我这里有一个长长的清单,列出了 go-to-market 团队做的事情,这里列举几个。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is you gotta research
zh: 一个是你要做研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, your customer, right?
zh: 比如,你的客户,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You gotta research your targets.
zh: 你要研究你的目标对象。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to find out information about targets.
zh: 你必须找到关于目标的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to find the right people at particular companies.
zh: 你必须找到特定公司里的合适的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to build POCs.
zh: 你必须构建 POC。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's, like, just a ton of stuff you have to do, right?
zh: 你要做的事情实在太多了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, I'm not gonna list everything here, but, like, what is the grand unifying theme?
zh: 所以,你知道,我不打算在这里列出所有事情,但是,大统一的主题是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, go-to-market is a data problem, right?
zh: 嗯,go-to-market 是一个数据问题,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have this, like, entire world of...
zh: 所以你有了这个,整个世界的……

speaker: Unknown
en: of what your product does, and then this entire world of all your potential customers, and you're just trying to learn and figure out what your world looks like.
zh: 你的产品是做什么的，然后是整个由所有潜在客户组成的世界，而你只是试图学习和弄清楚你的世界是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is my proposal.
zh: 所以这就是我的提议。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a data problem, and we have to solve it from a data perspective.
zh: 这是一个数据问题，我们必须从数据的角度来解决它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool, so okay, so what is the data that is relevant?
zh: 好的，那么，相关的是什么数据呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I propose that you need basically a live model of your world that agents can act on.
zh: 我提出，你基本上需要一个智能体可以据此行动的、关于你的世界的实时模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what does that mean?
zh: 那么这意味着什么呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, well, one is you have a ton of internal data, right?
zh: 好的，首先，你拥有大量内部数据，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's all this information that you know about your customers, about people that are at your company,
zh: 有所有这些你了解的关于你的客户、关于你公司里的人的信息，

speaker: Unknown
en: Data about how people use the product.
zh: 关于人们如何使用产品的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's internal data that you know.
zh: 那是你了解的内部数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's all sorts of external data.
zh: 然后还有各种各样的外部数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's over 60 million companies in the world, and there's billions of people, over a billion that are on LinkedIn, for example.
zh: 世界上有超过 6000 万家公司，有数十亿人，比如在 LinkedIn 上就有超过十亿人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all sorts of stuff is happening every day.
zh: 而且每天都在发生各种各样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's all this news.
zh: 有这么多新闻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you're building this data go-to-market system, it's important to keep in mind all the different sources that exist and are available to your agents.
zh: 所以当你构建这个数据驱动的市场进入系统时，重要的是要记住所有存在的、可供你的智能体使用的不同数据源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And cool, so I'm gonna go through, hopefully pretty fast, just all the different components of what we've built at EXA.
zh: 好，那么我接下来会，希望比较快地，把我们构建的各个组成部分全部过一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just for context, I've been really passionate about this for a long time.
zh: 先说明一下背景，我对这个话题充满热情已经很久了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So EXA was launched in the middle of 2023, and so we were post-GPT4, and...
zh: EXA 是在 2023 年年中推出的，当时我们处于 GPT-4 之后的时代，然后……

speaker: Unknown
en: GPT-4 was really incredible, because it could actually, even then, even though it's way worse than like Fable or whatever, like it could actually just automate entire parts of go-to-market.
zh: GPT-4 真的非常了不起，因为即使在那时，尽管它比如 Fable 之类的差得远，它实际上已经可以自动化市场进入的整个环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so from the beginning, I've been thinking about our go-to-market from a very, very AI agent first perspective.
zh: 所以从一开始，我就一直以一种非常、非常以 AI 智能体为先的视角来思考我们的市场进入策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're gonna go over two interfaces that we have that help us, and then two agents.
zh: 所以我们要过一遍两个帮助我们做到这一点的界面，然后是两个智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool, okay, the first is what we call our ICP dashboard.
zh: 好，第一个是我们所说的 ICP 仪表盘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the ICP dashboard is a product that we have internally that answers the question, like, what is our world?
zh: ICP 仪表盘是我们内部的一个产品，它回答这个问题，比如，我们的世界是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what is the world of customers and use cases that we care about?
zh: 比如，我们关心的客户和用例的世界是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we actually do is we go ahead and use EXA
zh: 而我们实际做的，就是直接使用 EXA

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, EXA is this arbitrarily powerful search engine for AI's essentially.
zh: 再说一次，EXA 本质上是这个为 AI 打造的无比强大的搜索引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we just classify basically every possible company that is inside of our total addressable market.
zh: 我们基本上对处于我们总体可触达市场之内的每一家可能的公司进行分类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I kind of blurred out some of the details on how much money we make from each category and stuff like that.
zh: 我把一些关于我们每个类别赚多少钱之类的细节模糊掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, we have categories like model providers, AI coding platforms, like say Cursor, go-to-market intelligence tools.
zh: 但我们有像模型提供商、AI 编程平台（比如 Cursor）、市场进入情报工具这样的类别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this makes up our TAM and we have an understanding of literally almost every company within those segments.
zh: 这构成了我们的 TAM，我们实际上了解这些细分领域内几乎每一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for each of those companies, we can deep dive, right?
zh: 然后对于其中每一家公司，我们都可以深入挖掘，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So here's the example of SpaceX.
zh: 这里是 SpaceX 的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can see how much annual spend we could anticipate them to have, then all this metadata about the company.
zh: 我们可以看到我们可以预期他们有多少年度支出，然后还有关于这家公司的所有这些元数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have a list of all the companies and then a ton of data about each company.
zh: 所以我们有一份所有公司的清单，然后有关于每家公司的大量数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we do this?
zh: 我们是怎么做到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, we're able to do this because EXA is this search engine.
zh: 再说一次，我们能做到这一点是因为 EXA 是这个搜索引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: We take the internet, we crawl it, we train embeddings to do web search really well.
zh: 我们抓取整个互联网，我们训练嵌入模型来把网页搜索做得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so basically, from a technical perspective, you can think about EXA as embeddings over the internet.
zh: 所以基本上，从技术角度来说，你可以把 EXA 想成互联网之上的嵌入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you have embeddings over the internet, you have this arbitrarily powerful semantic filtering and slicing and dicing of any type of data that you want.
zh: 而当你拥有了互联网之上的嵌入，你就可以对任何你想要的数据类型进行无比强大的语义过滤、切片和切分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we use that to generate this gigantic list of potential ICPs.
zh: 于是我们用它来生成这个巨大的潜在 ICP 清单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Next, we have a tool we call RequestLens.
zh: 接下来，我们有一个叫做 RequestLens 的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: RequestLens, what is RequestLens?
zh: RequestLens，什么是 RequestLens？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's basically a system where any time something significant happens with any of our customers, we're alerted.
zh: 嗯，它基本上是一个系统，任何时候我们的任何客户发生了什么重要的事情，我们都会收到警报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone signed up, someone used a ton of
zh: 有人注册了，有人使用了大量的

speaker: Unknown
en: Searches.
zh: 搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone stopped using searches.
zh: 有人停止使用搜索了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone showed up that we really, really care about.
zh: 有一个我们非常、非常在乎的人出现了。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these things are signals that we are notified about and that our team can act on.
zh: 所有这些都是我们会收到通知的信号，我们的团队可以据此采取行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are the two interfaces that we have, and then I'll go over two types of agents that we have.
zh: 这就是我们的两个界面，接下来我会介绍我们拥有的两种类型的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one is coding agents.
zh: 第一种是编程智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our go-to-market team...
zh: 所以我们的市场推广团队……

speaker: Unknown
en: is crazy, crazy, crazy deep on agents.
zh: 在智能体方面 crazy、crazy、crazy 地深入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our engineering team uses a lot of agents, but our go-to-market team is like, you could look at some of their devin spend and other agent spend, it's really freaking high.
zh: 我们的工程团队大量使用智能体，但我们的市场推广团队，你可以看看他们的 Devin 支出和其他智能体支出，真的高得离谱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's because everybody on our go-to-market team is constantly asking agents about our customers, we have like,
zh: 这是因为我们市场推广团队里的每个人都在不断地向智能体询问我们客户的情况，我们有，

speaker: Unknown
en: Account executives that build demos for our customers.
zh: 为客户构建演示的销售人员(Account Executive)。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just this crazy ecosystem where we have maybe a dozen different agents inside of our Slack, and anybody can use any of them.
zh: 这是一个 crazy 的生态系统，我们的 Slack 里大概有十几个不同的智能体，任何人都可以使用其中任何一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all have access to tons and tons of our internal data.
zh: 它们都可以访问海量海量的我们内部数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, anytime we want to dig deeper on account, anytime we want to make a demo, et cetera, we depend heavily on agents.
zh: 是的，任何时候我们想深入了解某个客户、任何时候我们想做演示等等，我们都高度依赖智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool, and then I want to talk about another really cool agent that I'm pretty proud of.
zh: 好，接下来我想谈谈另一个我觉得相当自豪的、非常酷的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: We call it JeffBot, or I call it JeffBot.
zh: 我们叫它 JeffBot,或者我把它叫做 JeffBot。

speaker: Unknown
en: JeffBot is an AI clone of myself as much as possible.
zh: JeffBot 是一个尽可能像我本人的 AI 克隆。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what is it?
zh: 那么它是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, basically, this winter break,
zh: 嗯，基本上，这个寒假期间，

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure a lot of you spent that break playing with Opus 4.5 and I was no different.
zh: 我相信你们中很多人都在那个假期里玩 Opus 4.5,我也不例外。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was in Mexico and I had a week off and so my goal with that week and with Opus 4.5 was to just try to make a digital clone of myself.
zh: 当时我在墨西哥，有一周的假期，所以我在那一周里用 Opus 4.5 的目标就是尝试做一个我自己的数字克隆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I did things like analyze
zh: 于是我做了诸如分析

speaker: Unknown
en: Like 760 of my emails to figure out what my email voice is.
zh: 我大约 760 封邮件的事情，来弄清楚我的邮件文风。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, oh, I use 18 words on average per email, and I like to end emails with best and not sincerely, like all that type of stuff, right?
zh: 比如，哦，我平均每封邮件用 18 个词，我喜欢用 best 而不是 sincerely 来结尾邮件，诸如此类的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I made like a voice for myself, and then I also made a decision-making framework.
zh: 所以我为自己做了一种文风，然后我还做了一个决策框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I made like a decision-making framework where I analyzed hundreds of decisions I've made in the past.
zh: 我做了一个决策框架，分析了我过去做出的数百个决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I analyzed them and I created evals.
zh: 我分析了它们，并创建了 evals。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually created evals from those decisions and calibrated this agent system to behave like myself.
zh: 所以我真的从那些决策中创建了 evals,并校准了这个智能体系统，让它表现得像我自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally I gave it read and write access to all the data that I personally have.
zh: 最后，我给了它对我个人所有数据的读写权限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a cool advantage to this because I basically have access to every single system at the company because I'm in the nice seat of having that.
zh: 而这有一个很酷的优势，因为我基本上可以访问公司的每一个系统，因为我处在拥有这种权限的很好的位置上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, yeah, this thing has access to everything.
zh: 所以，是的，这个东西可以访问一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically what happens is anybody at the company can use JeffBot
zh: 基本上发生的事情是，公司里的任何人都可以使用 JeffBot

speaker: Unknown
en: to create drafts of Slack messages that are basically like answers or decisions that are made.
zh: 来创建 Slack 消息的草稿，这些消息基本上就是回答或做出的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a huge, great thing.
zh: 这是一件非常棒的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our go-to-market team uses it to draft emails, for example.
zh: 比如，我们的市场推广团队用它来起草邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, so those are the systems that we have at Exa.
zh: 好了，这些就是我们在 Exa 拥有的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: It works pretty well.
